orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Sharma,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Alok Singh,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari
orders.text:
SA No.08/05 
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Sr. Advocate, for 
the appellant. 
 Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Sr. Adv. 
assisted by Mr. Prince Chauhan, 
Advocate, for respondent no.1. 
 Plaintiff Mr. Rajendra Singh and 
defendant/respondent no.1 Mangal 
Singh are the close relatives of each 
other. The dispute is regarding the 
cancellation of sale deed which was 
executed by Mr. Kripal Singh (father of 
Rajendra Singh) in favour of Mr. Mangal 
Singh on 22.8.1969. 
 It has been averred that the land 
was in the nature of Sirdari, so this sale 
deed could not have been executed. 
 The suit was perfectly decreed on 
19.11.2001, where-against the First 
Appeal No.10 of 2001 was preferred and 
it was allowed, in part, holding that Mr. 
Kripal Singh could have transferred only 
one-half of the questioned land which fell 
in his share. It may be added that the 
remaining half portion of land was owned 
by Smt. Tara Devi, the wife of Mr. Kesar 
Singh, who died intestate. 
 Feeling aggrieved, Mr. Rajendra 
Singh has come up in this second appeal. 
 In the backdrop of facts, as stated 
above, I am of the opinion, and wherefor 
learned Senior Counsel for the parties 
also do agree, that Mr. Rajendra Singh 
and Mr. Mangal Singh be called, in 
person, in the Court so that the matter 
may be referred for reconciliation in the 
Alternative Disputes Redressal Forum. 
 Ordered accordingly. 
 List on 30.8.2016 for the purpose. 
 
 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 
 10.08.2016 
Rdang

I.A. No. 4 of 2025
In
SA No. 155 of 2022
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. J.K. Pandey, holding brief of Mr. Piyush Garg, 
learned counsel for the appellants.
2. Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Sr. Advocate, assisted by 
Mr. Pavan Kumar Nath, learned counsel for the 
respondents.
3. There was the delay of 5749 days in filing the instant 
second appeal, which was condoned by this Court on 
12.03.2024. Against the order dated 12.03.2024, respondents 
filed a Special Leave to Appeal before the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court, which was disposed of by the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court on 18.11.2014 with the following directions:
 
 “While we are not inclined to interfere with the order 
passed by the High Court condoning the delay of 5749 
days in filing the second appeal, we direct the respondents 
to pay costs quantified at Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty 
Thousand Only) to the appellant herein within a period of 
three months from today.” 
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in 
compliance of the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s order, a 
demand draft of Rs. 50,000/- was sent through post to the 
respondents but the same was refused and thereafter, 
original demand draft is placed on record by way of 
application (I.A. No. 4 of 2025).
5. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that the 
validity period of demand draft was 3 months, and as such, 
the same is expired now. 
6. In such an eventuality, appellant is directed to place a
fresh demand draft or get the demand draft renewed within 
a week. 
7. Registry is directed to return back the demand draft 
to the learned counsel for the appellants. 
8. List on 25.06.2025.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 12.06.2025.
SKS
